title: Rohit and Kohli Set to Become First Indian Pair to Play 400 Matches Together at Lord's
excerpt: The duo will surpass the all-time Indian record of 391 matches held by Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid when they take the field in the series-deciding third ODI against England on Sunday.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will play their 400th match together on Sunday.
  • They will surpass the previous Indian record of 391 matches held by Tendulkar and Dravid.
  • The duo first played together on August 18, 2008, against Sri Lanka.
  • Rohit and Kohli have won the 2023 ODI World Cup and 2024 T20 World Cup together.
  • They are India's most dependable partnership, with 11 century partnerships in ODIs.
Historic Milestone at Lord's

›Tendulkar & Dravid Previous Indian record: 391 matches
›Against Sri Lanka First match together: August 18, 2008
›ODI World Cup wins: 2023, 2024
›Total matches played together: 399
  • Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli are set to become the first Indian pair to play 400 international matches together when they take the field in the third ODI against England at Lord's on Sunday.
  • The duo will surpass the previous Indian record of 391 matches held by Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid, having already equaled it during the Australia tour last year.
  • Rohit and Kohli first played together on August 18, 2008, against Sri Lanka at Dambulla — 18 years ago.
  • The pair have won the 2023 ODI World Cup and the 2024 T20 World Cup together, retiring from T20Is and Tests to focus exclusively on the 50-over format.

Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will reach a landmark that no other Indian batting pair has touched when they walk out together at Lord's on Sunday for the third and deciding ODI against England. The match will mark the 400th time the two have represented India in international cricket — across ODIs, Tests and T20Is — shattering the previous Indian record of 391 matches held by Sachin Tendulkar and Rahul Dravid.

The milestone arrives at a venue steeped in cricket history, with the series level at 1-1 and both batters in strong recent form.

18 Years and Counting

"Rohit remains the only batter to have scored three double centuries in ODIs."

Kohli and Rohit first played together on August 18, 2008, in an ODI against Sri Lanka at Dambulla. Kohli was making his international debut; Rohit was playing his early ODIs. In that match, the 19-year-old Kohli opened the innings and scored 12, while Rohit batted in the middle order for 19.

Since then, the pair have played together across 60 Tests, approximately 230 ODIs and 106 T20 internationals. They retired together from T20Is after clinching the 2024 T20 World Cup in Barbados and stepped away from Test cricket before the England tour earlier this year, choosing to concentrate on the format where they remain India's most dependable partnership.

The global record for most matches as a pair belongs to Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara and Mahela Jayawardene, who played 550 matches together. But among Indian pairs, no one comes close to the Rohit-Kohli partnership.

The Numbers Behind the Partnership

Kohli holds the record for the most ODI centuries in history with 51, having overtaken Tendulkar during the 2023 World Cup. Rohit remains the only batter to have scored three double centuries in ODIs. Together, they have shared 11 century partnerships in ODI cricket, putting them among the top ten pairs of all time in the format.

A Series Decider at the Home of Cricket

Sunday's match carries stakes beyond the personal milestone. India lost the first ODI but leveled the series in the second, setting up a decider at Lord's — a ground that holds emotional weight for Indian cricket. Kohli in particular has produced some of his finest innings at the venue.

"Playing 400 matches together is an amazing achievement for these two cricketers, and the duo have earned India numerous ICC trophies."

— Cricket Addictor

England, playing on home soil, will look to exploit seam-friendly conditions that have traditionally challenged visiting batters early in the innings. For India, the presence of both Rohit and Kohli at the top of the order provides a cushion that few international sides can match.

The Endgame

At 39 (Rohit) and 37 (Kohli), the pair are closer to the end of their careers than the beginning. Neither has announced a timeline for ODI retirement, but with the 2027 Champions Trophy and the 2027 ODI World Cup qualification cycle approaching, every appearance together adds to a partnership that has defined Indian cricket for nearly two decades.

For the Indian diaspora in London and across the UK — who have packed Lord's for the series — Sunday's match is a chance to witness history. When Rohit and Kohli stride to the crease together for the 400th time, they will do so as the most enduring batting partnership India has ever produced.
